applicable_when: The kernel is a tensor layout permutation: it reads from in_ptr0 with strides (4032000, 1, 32000, 128) — channel dim has stride=1 (fastest in memory) — but the current tile mapping puts the channel index y0 in YBLOCK (slow tile, varies across program_id(1)) and the spatial index x2 in XBLOCK (fast tile, varies across program_id(0)). This means adjacent threads in a warp access in_ptr0 at offsets separated by 128 floats (stride=128), causing catastrophically non-coalesced L1 loads. The 0% L1 hit rate and 97% L2 throughput confirm every load misses L1 and hammers L2. The fix is to swap the tile mapping so the channel dim (y0, stride=1 in in_ptr0) is covered by XBLOCK, enabling coalesced 128-byte sector reads.
